source.label: For real points with a logarithmic local count the Gram form on the cut grid has normalized largest eigenvalue of order the count

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: phi real, even, supported in [-L/2, L/2], continuously differentiable on the line with phi' absolutely continuous, B = int |phi''|, B2 = int |(phi^2)''|; grid tau_k = tau_0 + 2 pi k/L, I = [tau_0, tau_{d-1}], M = max(|tau_0|, |tau_{d-1}|); a locally finite multiset of real points with at most A log(|t| + 3) points, with multiplicity, in every closed interval [t, t+1]. Then for every real u supported on 0 <= k < d the sum over the points of m_gamma (v_gamma . u)^2, v_gamma = (phihat(gamma - tau_k))_k, converges and is at most L ||phi||_2^2 Lambda0 |u|^2 with Lambda0 = 2 A log(M + 5) (1 + (pi^2/6) B2/||phi||_2^2 + B^2 (c4/L + c3/(6 pi))/||phi||_2^2), c4 = sum (1 + log j) j^-4 < 1.16, c3 = sum (1 + log j) j^-3 < 1.41: the cut Gram form of an infinite real configuration is positive semidefinite with normalized largest eigenvalue at most Lambda0.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof: points within distance 1 of the interval by the Gram matrix of their vectors and a weighted Schur test with the decay of the transform of phi^2; the others by the pointwise tail of the Gram form localization and the count. It extends the real configuration bound from the flat window on the complete grid to these windows on a cut grid and to infinite configurations, with the logarithm of the count in place of a logarithm of the number of cells. A model statement; that the zeros of zeta are real points in this sense is the hypothesis to be proved.
claims.rationale: Shows that the eigenvalue premise of the lead on Weil's positivity follows, in the model, from the statement to be proved, so that the premise is a consequence of the goal and not an independent input.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof in the entry; the two series constants and one instance evaluated numerically.
notes.significance: Context: places an unproved premise as a consequence of the goal in a model. No novelty claimed.
notes.relationships: Extends the real configuration bound; uses the pair atom spectrum's bilinear identity and part (i) of the Gram form localization.

relationships: The inner products of the points' vectors are taken from its bilinear identity.
Its part (i) gives the decay used for phi and for phi^2, and the far points use its pointwise sum over the grid.
Its companion in the same setting: that proposition bounds the cut form of one off-axis pair from below, this lemma the real points' from above.
The same statement for the flat window on the complete grid, by the same method; this one treats smooth windows, the cut grid and infinite configurations.
